title: On calculating polar solvation energy of nonrigid proteins in the Poisson-Boltzmann theory
summary: The Poisson-Boltzmann (PB) theory is a cornerstone of implicit solvent models for electrostatic analysis, and has found a great success in various biomolecular applications. However, in calculating polar solvation energy, one should consider that the structure of the protein changes upon transition from vacuum to water phases. To address this, here we report for the first time a generalized PB framework capable of accommodating nonrigid conformational changes without suffering from self-energy artifacts.
